output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new vendor rule, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC, Corvane's automatic rule-pack update added a rule that blocks requests from the networking library our Android app uses on the password-login path. The first blocks were logged at 10:41. Every Android version dropped at that moment, including the 95% of users who don't have 6.14. The OS patch status made no difference. Quick-unlock is unaffected. About 41,300 installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully before, so these are real customers and not bots. Rolling back 6.14, reverting the password screen, raising bot sensitivity, or excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would not fix this. The last two would make it worse or hide it. Next step: ask Corvane today to set the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and the other rules on. Then check in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Ask Corvane to exempt the app's library signature permanently. Require testing of vendor rule changes. I'm fairly confident, and the data supports this.
